page: Microsoft Azure E80ids_v4 is an isolated virtual machine instance belonging to the XEIDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.3 GB of RAM per core, and includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 4152.66 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 96.48 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 25% tier. Conversely, single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range, while LLM text generation speeds are notably weak, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a resource density perspective, the E80ids_v4 offers a high-capacity memory footprint paired with substantial local SSD storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large datasets to reside in memory. However, the tradeoff lies in its moderate single-core clock speed of 2.6 GHz and the absence of GPU hardware, which limits its utility for real-time AI inference or graphics-heavy rendering.

This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational and non-relational database hosting, large-scale Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines. It is also well-suited for software compilation and build systems that can fully exploit its 80 dedicated vCPUs and high memory bandwidth.

It features 504.0 GB of RAM and 2458 GB of local SSD storage, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and excellent database operations, though single-core speeds and LLM text generation are average to poor due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Qualitatively, the instance offers high resource density for memory-heavy workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, Redis caching, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
